title: Progressive column pinning + responsive column priorities for dense & fluid tables
creator: Aria Patel
description: Goal: design a progressive column pinning and responsive column-priority system that reduces horizontal overflow, improves discoverability, and preserves keyboard/assistive navigation across density modes. This ticket covers: 1) a priority-based rule engine that automatically collapses or hides low-priority columns at smaller widths or high-density modes; 2) a lightweight pin/unpin affordance with drag-to-pin support and keyboard commands (Alt/Cmd+K to toggle pin state); 3) visible micro-interactions for pinning, pinned-column badges, and animated column collapse to help users track layout shifts; 4) accessibility: focus order preservation, announced layout changes for screenreaders, and explicit aria-controls for pin toggles; 5) tokens: spacing/typography mappings for compact/comfortable/cozy densities so pinned columns maintain readable tap targets; 6) interaction with virtualization: ensure pinned columns are rendered in the fixed column layer and continue to use KV row height heuristics so virtualization performance remains stable. Deliverables: Figma prototype (responsive constraints + keyboard flow), updated design tokens sheet, annotated interaction spec for eng, acceptance criteria for QA and accessibility audits.

Suggested engineering spike to validate fixed column render strategy (ENG-3219). Added GitHub issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/issues/3892

2026-03-12 - Design review: Feedback from Alice (PM): prioritize toggle state clarity and add an undo toast for accidental unpin actions. Feedback from Dev Lead (Ravi): prefer declarative 'column priority' metadata on column configs to let runtime decide visibility instead of hard-coded widths.

2026-03-12 - Marcus: Filed engineering spike ticket ENG-3310 to evaluate perf implications on continuous-batching workloads and virtualization. Spike ETA 1 week. PR placeholder for token updates: https://github.com/redwood-inference/design-system/pull/214

2026-03-12 - Aria: Added accessibility acceptance criteria: keyboard pin/unpin reachable within tabindex order, pinned columns announced with role=note on toggle, layout-change announcements when automatic collapse occurs, and contrast checks for pinned badges.
acceptance_criteria: Users can pin/unpin a column via mouse, drag, and keyboard (shortcut documented)
Automatic priority-based collapse reduces horizontal overflow without hiding user-pinned columns
Pinned columns render in the fixed layer and do not break virtualization performance budgets (95th percentile render < 40ms extra)
Accessible behavior: screenreader announces pin/unpin and automatic collapse; focus order preserved; undo toast available
Updated design tokens for spacing/typography per density are merged to design-system repo
